name: Ohio
summary: Statutes, constitution and admin code: the official LSC site codes.ohio.gov (UELMA-official) is robots-disallowed ('User-agent: * Disallow: /', policy 2026-10-17), so there is no tier-1 text route; use Justia (2025 Ohio Revised Code; constitution per section; WebFetch only) and Cornell LII for the Administrative Code (colon→hyphen slugs; can lag by years and carries redline text), always disclosed. Court rules are long full-set PDFs on supremecourt.ohio.gov that WebFetch cuts off early (Civ.R. text stops at Rule 5) — read them with fetch_doc.py or a corpus. Case law: Ohio's public-domain webcite (2023-Ohio-3005, ¶ pinpoints) maps to a PDF URL once the court is known (rod/docs/pdf/{0|district}/{year}/{webcite}.pdf, county→district table in the record); the Reporter of Decisions search (1992-, POST only, and the year range must be set explicitly or it returns 0 rows) resolves webcites, Ohio St.3d cites and case numbers, and finds 'appeals not accepted for review' dispositions by the lower court's webcite. The Register of Ohio and legislature.ohio.gov fail TLS from the shell.

citation_map.notes: Ohio style (Supreme Court of Ohio Writing Manual, from memory) differs from Bluebook: 'R.C. 2305.10' (no §), 'Ohio Adm.Code 3701-17-01', 'Civ.R. 12(B)(6)' with capital division letters, 'Section 16, Article I, Ohio Constitution' (section first), and case cites 'Name, 172 Ohio St.3d 471, 2023-Ohio-3005, ¶ 20' or for appeals 'Name, 2022-Ohio-1555, ¶ 10 (7th Dist.)'; pre-2023 manual form '7th Dist. Jefferson No. 21 JE 0013, 2022-Ohio-1555'. Pinpoint is the ¶ number, which is the same in the slip PDF, the official-version PDF and Ohio St.3d (Rep.Op.R. 2.5 requires numbered paragraphs). Rep.Op.R. 3.4: all court-of-appeals opinions issued after May 1, 2002 may be cited regardless of publication. The webcite alone does not name the court; the URL folder needs it: 0 = Supreme Court, 1-12 = district, 13 = Court of Claims. Take the district from the '(Nth Dist.)' parenthetical or the county ('Jefferson App. No.') via the county table in oh-opinions-rod; otherwise resolve with the ROD WebCite search. Routing guards: bare 'Civ.R. 12', 'Evid.R. 702', 'App.R. 26', 'Crim.R. 11' are Ohio house style, but a bare 'Rule 12' or a federal-rule cite must not route here — require the Ohio abbreviation or Ohio context. 'Revised Code' alone also names Washington's code (Revised Code of Washington): route 'R.C. NNNN.NN' (Ohio sections always contain a dot) or 'of the Revised Code' only with Ohio context. The webcite form YYYY-Ohio-N is unique to Ohio and routes on its own. Ranges like 'R.C. 2305.10 to 2305.12' or 'R.C. 2305.10-.12': take the first section; the regex stops at the first section number. 'Section 1.42' of the Revised Code is valid (Title 1 General Provisions). OAC rules may carry a colon in the agency number (4901:1-10-01) — keep it in the URL. Superintendence Rules were renumbered effective July 1, 2026 (e.g. old Sup.R. 44 → 11.09); older opinions cite old numbers. CourtListener ids (ohio, ohioctapp, ohioctcl) are from memory and unverified. ROUTING after the 2026-10-17 policy: codes.ohio.gov is robots-disallowed, so R.C. → oh-orc-justia, Ohio Const. → oh-constitution-justia, Ohio Adm.Code → oh-oac-lii (all tier 2, disclosed); the blocked official rows stay last in routes_to for link reference only. Regex extended 2026-10-17 for chapter cites ('R.C. Chapter 2744') and 'Ohio Const., Art. I, Sec. 16'. Bare 'OAC …' is shared with the Oklahoma Administrative Code (also colon-numbered), so it routes here only once Ohio is established.

sources.title: Ohio Revised Code (codes.ohio.gov)
sources.official_status_evidence: https://codes.ohio.gov/about: UELMA (R.C. 149.21 to 149.27) designates LSC official publisher; electronic Revised Code and Administrative Code 'are official publications (R.C. 149.21 and 149.22)'. Authenticated PDF per section; the stamp verifies integrity, not freedom from error. Unannotated; repeals and court invalidations are not noted.
sources.coverage: Current Revised Code, one page per section (Titles 1-63 incl. Title 1 General Provisions), with prior versions for some sections; per-section authenticated PDF; chapter pages hold the full text of every section in the chapter.

access.pattern_rules: section = the R.C. number verbatim with its dot and any letter (2305.10, 2903.01, 1.42, 2305.131). Short form https://codes.ohio.gov/orc/{section} redirects to the same page. Chapter page: /ohio-revised-code/chapter-{chapter} (full text of all sections; 2305 = 233K chars). Title index: /ohio-revised-code/title-{title} lists chapters only (no section ranges); the chapter is the part before the dot, so no index hop is needed. Authenticated PDF: /assets/laws/revised-code/authenticated/{title}/{chapter}/{section}/{M-D-YYYY effective}/{section}-{M-D-YYYY}.pdf — the date segment is not derivable; take the 'Download Authenticated PDF' link from the section page.

automation.robots_txt: 200 text/plain, one line 'User-agent: * Disallow: /' (no newline); treated as Disallow: / for all agents (policy 2026-10-17)
automation.notes: BLOCKED for every route (incl. the /orc/ short form and /assets/… authenticated PDFs). Use oh-orc-justia (tier 2, disclose it). Earlier 2026-10-16 fetches were made before the policy decision and must not be repeated.

Authenticated PDF /assets/laws/revised-code/authenticated/23/2305/2305.10/8-3-2006/2305.10-8-3-2006.pdf: 3 pp, body present. | Re-confirmed blocked 2026-10-17: fetch_doc check: 'REFUSED: robots.txt on codes.ohio.gov disallows ... sources.notes: Policy decision 2026-10-17 (coordinator): codes.ohio.gov's one-line robots.txt 'User-agent: * Disallow: /' is read by its evident intent — disallow all automation — so this host is BLOCKED for every route (fetch_doc.py refuses it; WebFetch is not used on it). This hurts: under Ohio's UELMA (R.C. 149.21-149.27) LSC's codes.ohio.gov text is the official, authenticated publication, and there is now no tier-1 text route. URL patterns are kept for reference/linking only. No bulk download or public statute API found (WebSearch for bulk XML/API returned only page URLs). No tier-1 statute text route remains; Cornell LII and public.law have no Revised Code.

Cuyahoga No.') mapped by this fixed table — 1 = Hamilton; 2 = Champaign, Clark, Darke, Greene, Miami, Montgomery; 3 = Allen, Auglaize, Crawford, Defiance, Hancock, Hardin, Henry, Logan, Marion, Mercer, Paulding, Putnam, Seneca, Shelby, Union, Van Wert, Wyandot; 4 = Adams, Athens, Gallia, Highland, Hocking, Jackson, Lawrence, Meigs, Pickaway, Pike, Ross, Scioto, Vinton, Washington; 5 = Ashland, Coshocton, Delaware, Fairfield, Guernsey, Holmes, Knox, Licking, Morgan, Morrow, Muskingum, Perry, Richland, Stark, Tuscarawas; 6 = Erie, Fulton, Huron, Lucas, Ottawa, Sandusky, Williams, Wood; 7 = Belmont, Carroll, Columbiana, Harrison, Jefferson, Mahoning, Monroe, Noble; 8 = Cuyahoga; 9 = Lorain, Medina, Summit, Wayne; 10 = Franklin; 11 = Ashtabula, Geauga, Lake, Portage, Trumbull; 12 = Brown, Butler, Clermont, Clinton, Fayette, Madison, Preble, Warren. ASP.NET form at https://www.supremecourt.ohio.gov/rod/docs/ (POST only; a plain GET with the field names is ignored and returns the default newest-first listing, and a GET carrying __VIEWSTATE returns 404). POST fields (prefix ctl00$MainContent$): tbQueryText (full text, quotes for phrases), ddlCourt (0 Supreme Court, 1-12 districts, 13 Court of Claims, 98 Misc., 99 All Sources, 100 All District Courts), ddlDecidedYearMin/Max (1992-2026), ddlCounty, tbCaseNumber, tbAuthor, tbWebCiteYear + tbWebCiteNumber (unique lookup, other filters ignored), tbCitation (e.g. '172 Ohio St.3d 471' → webcite), ddlRowsPerPage, btnSubmit=Submit, plus the page's hidden __VIEWSTATE/__VIEWSTATEGENERATOR.
